newsitem.title: THAILAND: Car maker BMW sees big potential in Asia-Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Car maker BMW sees big potential in Asia-Pacific.

text.p: The chairman of German car maker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG said on Thursday the car market in the Asia-Pacific region will continue to grow rapidly over the medium-term.

BMW chairman Bernd Pischetsrieder told Reuters in an interview he expects the car market in the Asia-Pacific region to grow by 5 percent to 10 percent per year over the long term -- much faster than the European and U.S. car markets.
"This is the fastest growing area in the world. In 25 years time, Southeast Asia, excluding Japan, will have the size of the European market of about eight million cars a year," he said.
The region's rapidly growing economies also provide strong demand for the luxury auto market.

"In the long-term, the luxury segment in this area should grow faster than the overall market because of growing wealth. This is unique to Asia, and southeast Asia in particular," Pischetsrieder said.
Kay Segler, managing director of BMW Asia, said BMW's total car sales in Asian markets including Japan was currently about 60,000 units per year, accounting for 10 percent of BMW car sales worldwide.
"Asian markets already have a major share (of BMW car sales) and the share will continue to increase," Segler told Reuters.
Despite the fast growing car market of the Asian region, BMW has no plan for new investments to expand production capacity.

"Our main objective (in the region) is to use our existing capacity more efficiently. I don't foresee us having a major investment in capacity which we don't already have...in the region," Pischetsrieder said.
He said BMW regards Thailand as good candidate to be a major base in the region due to the country's high economic growth and good infrastructure for the car manufacturing industry.

BMW on Thursday said the company and its long-time Thai partner, the Yontrakit Group, agreed to form a joint venture to take over the wholesale function for BMW cars and motorcycles from the beginning of 1997.
The new company, called BMW Thailand, will be held 51 percent by Yontrakit, 49 percent by BMW. The managing director will come from BMW management.
BMW Thailand will be the third sales organisation managed directly by the German automotive group in Asia. The other two are in Japan and Korea.
BMW said it expects the total car market in Thailand to exceed 800,000 vehicles in 2000.
"We see a bright future in Thailand for the car industry. We expect the luxury car market to develop in line with rising living standards in Thailand over the next years," Pischetsrieder said.
